clue.text: Show amusement about one as daft as a brush, say

definitions.text: as daft as a brush, say

indicators.note: about means going round something, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to show amusement is to smile
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone grins at a person who is being very silly.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside SMILE to make SIMILE. 'As daft as a brush' is a British phrase meaning very silly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase compares a person to a brush using 'as', which makes it an example of a figure of speech built on comparison.

clue.text: End bombardment with a delicate tennis stroke

parts.note: to end something is to stop it
a volley is a barrage of shots or missiles

explanation.surface: A tennis player ends an onslaught of hard hitting with a soft touch.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis this shot is hit before the ball bounces and dies just over the net, a gentle touch rather than power.

clue.text: Fruit from Middle East — large ones? Not half!

indicators.note: not half says only half of the word survives, the rest is dropped

parts.note: standard abbreviation for the Middle East
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the first half of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether fruit from the Middle East is big, and gets the emphatic British reply 'Not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it tells you to keep only half of 'ones'.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a large juicy fruit of the gourd family, such as a cantaloupe or watermelon.

clue.text: Girl soprano, Jenny, for example

parts.note: Jenny Lind, the nineteenth-century Swedish soprano
say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: A young singer, Jenny, is offered as an example of a soprano.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Lind, the 'Swedish Nightingale', was a famous Victorian-era soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Lindsay is a female first name, so it is an instance of a girl's name.

clue.text: Convincing Roman Catholic to admit weakness? Just the opposite

indicators.text: to admit weakness? Just the opposite
indicators.note: admit means let in, and just the opposite swaps which piece holds and which is held

parts.note: a foible is a minor weakness of character
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Persuading a Catholic to confess a failing, though it turns out the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, RC holds the weakness; the reversal at the end means the weakness holds RC: FO(RC)IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A forcible argument is powerful and compelling, which is what convincing means.

clue.text: Peace offering from bachelor in 7 around 5

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the cross-references cannot be resolved from this grid, where 7 and 5 are other entries
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: A single man makes a gesture of reconciliation.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published is faulty: its numbered references point to entries in this grid that cannot supply the letters, so only the bachelor and the definition can be checked.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding out a sprig from the olive tree is the traditional symbol of seeking peace, so the phrase means a conciliatory gesture.

clue.text: A Romany leader entering Irish county in a mobile home

indicators.note: entering means going inside something else

parts.note: Cavan is a county in the Republic of Ireland
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Romany chief arrives in County Cavan living in a mobile home.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair goes in after the county's first letter, not at its middle. The Romany travellers of the surface fit the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a towed vehicle equipped for living in, so it is a home on wheels.

clue.text: Outspoken actors in show

parts.note: broad can mean plain-spoken or coarse
the actors in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: Plain-speaking performers appear in a production.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a programme put out on radio or television, so it is a show.

clue.text: Bridge player, poorest having lost pounds

indicators.note: having lost says something is taken away from the word

parts.note: least as in lowest or worst in quality
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: The weakest player at the bridge table has lost money.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from LEAST. The four players at bridge are named after compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four partnership seats are North, South, East and West, so one player is called by that compass point.

clue.text: Old boy stretched, in shape

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
something stretched is long

explanation.surface: A former pupil has been stretched out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle longer than it is wide, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Nonsense written in columns exposing clowns

indicators.note: written in means put inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: piers are supporting pillars
rot is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Rubbish printed in newspaper columns reveals who the fools are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columns' suggests newspaper columns, but here they are architectural supports.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrots are the white-faced, loose-costumed comic performers of French pantomime and seaside shows.

clue.text: Goddess seen in play

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love
seen and observed are synonyms

explanation.surface: The goddess makes an appearance in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a 1950 verse comedy by Christopher Fry.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus Observed is the title of a stage comedy by the English dramatist Christopher Fry.

clue.text: Dog's plus point husband discovered during spring

indicators.note: discovered during means found within, so these pieces sit inside another

parts.note: to spring is to bound or leap
an asset is an advantage
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A dog's best feature is that it found its owner's husband in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is the verb for leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset hound is a short-legged, long-eared breed of scent hound.

clue.text: Property not supposed to be taken to car

parts.note: something genuine, not merely supposed, is real
an estate is the British term for a station wagon

explanation.surface: Land or buildings are, unexpectedly, to be carted off by car.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings, the legal term for immovable property.

clue.text: Eminent newspaper framed by the US actress, Myrna

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded on both sides, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Myrna Loy, the Hollywood star of The Thin Man films
FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A distinguished newspaper puts a photograph of Myrna Loy round itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a London daily, abbreviated FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means elevated in rank or character, as eminent does.

clue.text: Pick up food for bird

parts.note: to field is to gather up the ball in cricket or baseball
fare is food or provisions

explanation.surface: Someone collects something to eat for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush that winters in Britain from northern Europe.

clue.text: Sort of beer — not lagers, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are set out in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Describing a particular beer by saying, strangely, that it is no lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' could suggest taking odd letters, but every letter of the two words is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong ale is a category of high-alcohol British beer, so it is a type of beer.

clue.text: Ivy, perhaps, always pale and sickly-looking

parts.note: ever means always
a person looking green is pale and nauseous

explanation.surface: A plant, or a woman called Ivy, is forever looking ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy could be a woman's name, making the sickly look a description of her.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy keeps its leaves all year, so it is an example of a plant that never loses its foliage.

clue.text: Attempt, with wife, to share expenses equally

parts.note: a go is a try
'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife, from duchess

explanation.surface: A man and his wife try to split the bill fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' meaning wife comes from Cockney 'duchess'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means each person pays for their own share, so costs are divided evenly.

clue.text: From Soho, telephone the Savoy, perhaps

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: Phoning a famous London establishment from the Soho district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is a grand hotel on the Strand in London, near Soho.
explanation.definitionFit: The Savoy is a well-known luxury London establishment offering rooms to guests, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Spend time relaxing in lodge

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to idle away time casually
second meaning: to live or stay somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds in a holiday lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to loiter at leisure and, informally, to reside or be staying at a place.

clue.text: Our host, hidden away, poured drinks

indicators.note: away here means gone astray, out of their places, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The host had disappeared, so someone else served the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden away' reads as one phrase, but 'hidden' is fodder and 'away' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To do the honours is the idiom for acting as host, especially serving food or drink.

clue.text: Worried about vessel

indicators.note: worried means agitated or shaken about, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a link word here, but it is the material to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, which is a type of naval craft.

clue.text: Man, perhaps, in his Levi's

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A man, wearing his jeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea; the capital at the start of the clue hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea, so Man is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Begin a journey in craft with sturdy exterior

indicators.note: with an exterior means wrapped in an outer layer, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: stout means sturdy and strongly built
art means skill or craft

explanation.surface: Setting off on a voyage in a boat with a strong hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat to go with the journey, but here it means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: To start out is the phrasal verb for setting off on a trip or embarking on something.

clue.text: Trumpet playing drowned by cor anglais, initially

indicators.note: drowned by means submerged in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
an actor who is playing is on stage

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A trumpet's sound is swamped by a cor anglais in the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The trumpet is not the instrument but the trumpet-shaped centre of a daffodil.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany the corona is the trumpet-shaped central part of a daffodil or narcissus flower.

clue.text: Looks at head, uneasy in a visor

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it

indicators.note: uneasy means unsettled, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a worried-looking head wearing a visor.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeshade is a peaked band worn on the forehead to keep light out of the eyes, like a visor.

clue.text: Sculpted figure of Nehru finally acquired by nation

indicators.note: acquired by means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a state is a nation

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of the name

explanation.surface: A country buys a sculpture of Nehru, India's first prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast three-dimensional representation of a person or animal.
